claim: Abnormal accumulations of histones are sufficient to induce whole-genome duplications (WGDs) in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
source: Here, we show in Saccharomyces cerevisiae that abnormal accumulations of histones are sufficient to induce WGDs.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript including FACS analysis showing diploid populations arising from histone overexpression.

claim: High levels of histones reduce the incorporation of histone variant H2A.Z to chromatin.
source: Our results link these WGDs to a reduced incorporation of the histone variant H2A.Z to chromatin.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 5a showing decreased H2A.Z at pericentromeric regions.

claim: High levels of histones promote Swe1WEE1 stabilization.
source: Moreover, we show that high levels of histones promote Swe1WEE1 stabilisation thereby triggering the phosphorylation and inhibition of Cdc28CDK1 through a mechanism different of the canonical DNA damage response.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6d showing Swe1 stabilization in rad53-AID lsm1∆ treated cells.

claim: High levels of histones trigger phosphorylation and inhibition of Cdc28CDK1.
source: Moreover, we show that high levels of histones promote Swe1WEE1 stabilisation thereby triggering the phosphorylation and inhibition of Cdc28CDK1 through a mechanism different of the canonical DNA damage response.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by Western blot data in Figures 6e and 7d showing Cdc28 phosphorylation.

claim: The Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation induced by high histone levels occurs through a mechanism different from the canonical DNA damage response.
source: Moreover, we show that high levels of histones promote Swe1WEE1 stabilisation thereby triggering the phosphorylation and inhibition of Cdc28CDK1 through a mechanism different of the canonical DNA damage response.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by data in Figure 6f showing that MEC1 deletion does not abolish Cdc28 phosphorylation.

claim: Higher eukaryotes are unable to survive without histones.
source: Higher eukaryotes are unable to survive without histones and possess several alternative pathways to ensure enough histones during replication (Cook et al., 2011; Groth et al., 2005; Marzluff et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Cells can modulate cell cycle progression when histones become limiting to ensure faithful chromatin replication and avoid genome instability.
source: Cells can also modulate cell cycle progression when histones become limiting to ensure the faithful replication of chromatin and avoid genome instability (Groth et al., 2007; Günesdogan et al., 2014; Murillo-Pineda et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Histone excess has been linked to genome instability.
source: Histone excess has also been linked to genome instability and to a wide variety of processes in the cell including DNA repair and life span, which probably explains why all eukaryotes have several redundant pathways that ensure the absence of free histones beyond replication (Au et al., 2008; Castillo et al., 2007; Feser et al., 2010; Gunjan and Verreault, 2003; Singh et al., 2010; Takayama et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: All eukaryotes have several redundant pathways that ensure the absence of free histones beyond replication.
source: Histone excess has also been linked to genome instability and to a wide variety of processes in the cell including DNA repair and life span, which probably explains why all eukaryotes have several redundant pathways that ensure the absence of free histones beyond replication (Au et al., 2008; Castillo et al., 2007; Feser et al., 2010; Gunjan and Verreault, 2003; Singh et al., 2010; Takayama et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: Saccharomyces cerevisiae has two major checkpoints able to block cells prior to mitosis: the DNA damage response (DDR) and the spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC).
source: Saccharomyces cerevisiae like most eukaryotic cells has two major checkpoints able to block cells prior to mitosis: the DNA damage response (DDR) (Ciccia and Elledge, 2010) and the spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC) (Musacchio and Salmon, 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature and represents established knowledge.

claim: The DDR and SAC can block mitosis by inhibiting the cleavage and degradation of Scc1RAD21 through stabilization of Pds1Securin.
source: Both of them are able to perform this block inhibiting the cleavage and degradation of the kleisin subunit of the cohesin complex Scc1RAD21. This inhibition takes place through a stabilisation of Pds1Securin either by phosphorylation (DDR) (Sanchez et al., 1999) or by preventing its degradation through the APC (DDR and SAC) (Agarwal et al., 2003; London and Biggins, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The DDR can block mitosis through phosphorylation and inhibition of Cdc28CDK1 at Tyr19.
source: The DDR can also block mitosis through the phosphorylation and inhibition of the G2/M cyclin-dependent kinase Cdc28CDK1 at Tyr19 (15 in humans) that plays a key role during mitosis (Agarwal and Cohen-Fix, 2002; Rahal and Amon, 2008; Zhang et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The morphogenesis checkpoint delays cell-cycle progression when the actin cytoskeleton is perturbed.
source: Besides these well-characterised checkpoints, studies in S. cerevisiae have revealed an additional checkpoint able to respond to actin cytoskeleton perturbations called the morphogenesis checkpoint, which delays cell-cycle progression when the actin cytoskeleton is perturbed (Lew, 2000; McMillan et al., 2002; Sakchaisri et al., 2004; Sia et al., 1998).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The morphogenesis checkpoint stabilizes Swe1WEE1, which promotes phosphorylation of Cdc28CDK1 at Tyr19.
source: This checkpoint is able to stabilise Swe1WEE1, a kinase able to promote a phosphorylation on Tyr19 of Cdc28CDK1 (Tyr15 in humans) that inhibits its activity and results in a delay on the metaphase to anaphase transition (Lianga et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Swe1WEE1 is expressed during replication and degraded before mitosis through hyperphosphorylation and proteasomal destruction.
source: Swe1WEE1 is present in lower and higher eukaryotes during an unperturbed cell cycle. This kinase is expressed during replication and degraded before mitosis in a mechanism that involves the action of several kinases that promote Swe1WEE1 hyperphosphorylation and trigger its ubiquitination and subsequent destruction by the proteasome (Howell and Lew, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Swe1WEE1 can be stabilized upon DNA damage.
source: Swe1WEE1 can also be stabilised upon DNA damage (Palou et al., 2015) and in response to certain types of stress (Chauhan et al., 2015; George et al., 2007; King et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Swe1WEE1 physically interacts with histone H2B and promotes its phosphorylation.
source: Interestingly, Swe1WEE1 was quite recently shown to be able to physically interact with histone H2B and promote its phosphorylation. This phosphorylation is conserved from yeasts to humans and seems to play an important role in the repression of histone transcription at the end of S-phase (Mahajan et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: H2B phosphorylation by Swe1WEE1 is conserved from yeasts to humans.
source: Interestingly, Swe1WEE1 was quite recently shown to be able to physically interact with histone H2B and promote its phosphorylation. This phosphorylation is conserved from yeasts to humans and seems to play an important role in the repression of histone transcription at the end of S-phase (Mahajan et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Deletion of the NEG regulatory site in the HTA1-HTB1 cluster interferes with normal repression of histones H2A and H2B by the HIR complex.
source: Deletion of the NEG regulatory site (∆NEG) in the HTA1-HTB1 cluster interferes with the normal repression of histones H2A and H2B by the HIR complex and leads to their persistent transcription beyond S-phase (Figure 1a) (Eriksson et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Transformation of rad53K227A or tom1∆ cells with CEN-HTA1-HTB1∆NEG generates a large number of small colonies with severe growth defects and a small population of large colonies that grow almost like wild-type cells.
source: When transformed in rad53K227A or tom1∆ cells, this construct generated a large number of small colonies that experienced severe growth defects and a small population of large colonies able to grow almost like wild-type cells (Figure 1b) (between 2–4 × 10−2, raw numbers are in the additional source data file for Figure 1b) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b and Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Large colonies from rad53K227A or tom1∆ cells transformed with CEN-HTA1-HTB1∆NEG have experienced a WGD and became diploid.
source: FACS analysis of these two populations revealed that large colonies had experienced a WGD and became diploid (Figure 1b)
evidence: This statement is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: WGDs from histone overexpression were not observed in wild-type cells transformed with CEN-HTA1-HTB1∆NEG.
source: This effect was not observed in wild-type cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: WGDs induced by histone overexpression are not specific for histones H2A and H2B.
source: This effect was not observed in wild-type cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b) and was not specific for the overexpression of histones H2A and H2B (Figure 1c).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1c demonstrating that overexpression of H3/H4 also induces WGDs.

claim: Diploids arising from histone overexpression are able to tolerate better high levels of histones than haploids.
source: Growth analysis of small (n) and big colonies (2 n) in the rad53K227A mutant confirmed that diploids are able to tolerate better high levels of histones (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This statement is supported by growth analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Wild-type cells transformed with a high-copy vector containing HTA1-HTB1∆NEG (2µ∆NEG) give rise to a significant number of cells (around 1 × 10−2) that have experienced a WGD.
source: Cells transformed with a high-copy vector that contains the HTA1-HTB1∆NEG construct (2µ∆NEG) vector gave rise to a significant number of cells (around 1 × 10−2, source data file for Figure 1b) that have experienced a WGD (Figure 1d).
evidence: This statement is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: The 2µ∆NEG construct increases histone H2B mRNA by 50%.
source: This construct increases by 50% the amount of histone H2B mRNA but does not induce a detectable change in the amounts of total histone H2B protein (Figure 1e and f).
evidence: This statement is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: The 2µ∆NEG construct does not induce a detectable change in the amounts of total histone H2B protein.
source: This construct increases by 50% the amount of histone H2B mRNA but does not induce a detectable change in the amounts of total histone H2B protein (Figure 1e and f).
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: Diploids arising from 2µ∆NEG transformation were perfectly viable and did not show any major chromosome reorganization compared to haploid or diploid strains obtained by cross.
source: Diploids were perfectly viable, did not show any major chromosome reorganisation when compared to a haploid or diploid strain obtained by cross (Figure 1g)
evidence: This statement is supported by karyotype analysis shown in Figure 1g.

claim: Diploids arising from 2µ∆NEG transformation were able to form triploids when crossed with a strain from the opposite mating type.
source: Diploids were perfectly viable, did not show any major chromosome reorganisation when compared to a haploid or diploid strain obtained by cross (Figure 1g) and were able to form triploids when crossed with a strain from the opposite mating type (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: This statement is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1e.

claim: Diploids arising from 2µ∆NEG transformation still had a small growth advantage when compared to haploids in wild-type conditions.
source: Diploids still had a small growth advantage when compared to haploids in wild-type conditions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1f).
evidence: This statement is supported by growth data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1f.

claim: WGDs were never detected in wild-type cells transformed with an empty vector (more than 2.2 × 10² colonies analysed by FACS).
source: WGDs were never detected in wild-type cells transformed with an empty vector (more than 2.2 × 102 colonies analysed by FACS).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data from FACS analysis of control cells.

claim: Most haploid cells transformed with 2µ∆NEG turn into a diploid state in 48–96 hr after inoculation in liquid from a petri dish plate.
source: Time course experiments with these cells revealed that most of them usually turned into a diploid state in 48–96 hr after inoculation in liquid from a petri dish plate (colonies have already grown for 5 days in the plate) (Figure 2a).
evidence: This statement is supported by time course FACS data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Cells transformed with 2µ∆NEG show a large population of non-dividing cells and a significant decrease in the number of cells that have started to separate their chromosomes.
source: Cell cycle distribution of these haploids transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector in a strain carrying several tags to follow kinetochores (Mtw1-mCHERRY), centrosomes (Spc42-CFP) and tubulin (TUB1-GFP)) revealed a large population of non-dividing cells as well as a significant decrease in the number of cells that have started to separate their chromosomes (Figure 2b).
evidence: This statement is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: In some cells transformed with 2µ∆NEG, the whole spindle apparatus was able to traverse to the daughter cell before segregation.
source: Interestingly, in some of these cells we observed that the whole spindle apparatus was able to traverse to the daughter cell before segregation (Figure 2c).
evidence: This statement is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Live microscopy of cells transformed with 2µ∆NEG confirmed a large population of non-dividing cells and a significant number of cells (18% vs 3% in control) in which the nucleus remained undivided for several hours.
source: This analysis confirmed a large population of non-dividing cells in the strain transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector, consistent with previous observations (Morillo-Huesca et al., 2010), and a significant number of cells (18% vs 3% in the control strain) in which the nucleus remained undivided for several hours (Figure 2d, first panel and source data file for Figure 2d).
evidence: This statement is supported by live microscopy data shown in Figure 2d and quantification in the source data file.

claim: A small proportion of cells transformed with 2µ∆NEG (8%) showed nuclear migration to the daughter cell before mitosis.
source: The first one was a small proportion of cells (8%) in which the nucleus migrated to the daughter cell before mitosis (Figure 2d, second panel).
evidence: This statement is supported by live microscopy data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Some cells transformed with 2µ∆NEG (1%) undergo aberrant mitosis in which both nuclei remain trapped in the daughter, generating a binucleated cell.
source: The second phenotype involved a combination of the two phenomena previously described and led on some occasions (1%) to an aberrant mitosis in which both nuclei remain trapped in the daughter, generating a binucleated cell (Figure 2d, third panel).
evidence: This statement is supported by live microscopy data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Aberrant mitosis in which the daughter keeps all the genetic material only takes place in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector and never in cells with an empty vector.
source: These movies confirmed that aberrant mitosis in which the daughter (never observed in the mother) keeps all the genetic material only take place in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector.
evidence: This statement is supported by live microscopy data comparing cells with 2µ∆NEG versus empty vector.

claim: Binucleated cells arising from aberrant mitosis can undergo a second cell division in which the two nuclear masses are split between mother and daughter.
source: In one of these events, we were able to follow a second cell division of one of these binucleated cells in which the two nuclear masses were split between the mother and the daughter (Figure 2e).
evidence: This statement is supported by live microscopy data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: The rad53-AID degron is functional as indicated by low levels of Rad53 after one hour of treatment with 500 µM NAA.
source: The rad53-AID degron was fully functional as indicated by the low level of Rad53 after one hour of treatment with 500 µM NAA (1-Naphthaleneacetic acid, NAA) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a.

claim: rad53-AID mutant cells are sensitive to histone overexpression.
source: rad53-AID mutant cells were sensitive to histone overexpression and deletion of LSM1 was lethal in these cells in the presence of Auxin (Figure 3—figure supplement 1b and c).
evidence: This statement is supported by plate growth assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Deletion of LSM1 is lethal in rad53-AID cells in the presence of Auxin.
source: rad53-AID mutant cells were sensitive to histone overexpression and deletion of LSM1 was lethal in these cells in the presence of Auxin (Figure 3—figure supplement 1b and c).
evidence: This statement is supported by plate growth assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1c.

claim: 4 hr of Auxin treatment reduces 90% of cell viability in rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells.
source: Indeed, 4 hr of Auxin treatment was sufficient to reduce 90% of cell viability (Figure 3—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This statement is supported by colony formation assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1d.

claim: The lethality of rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells after Auxin treatment is much higher than that observed in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG.
source: This lethality was much higher than the one observed in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG (Figure 3—figure supplement 1e) indicating that this conditional system was much more toxic for the cell.
evidence: This statement is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1e.

claim: Rad53 depletion per se has little or no effect on histone accumulation.
source: Quantification of histone levels indicated that Rad53 depletion per se had little or no effect on histone accumulation but did increase histone levels in an lsm1∆ background (Figure 3b).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification of purified histones shown in Figure 3b.

claim: Rad53 depletion increases histone levels in an lsm1∆ background.
source: Quantification of histone levels indicated that Rad53 depletion per se had little or no effect on histone accumulation but did increase histone levels in an lsm1∆ background (Figure 3b).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification of purified histones shown in Figure 3b.

claim: rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells treated with NAA show a significant increase of canonical histones compared to histone H2A.Z levels.
source: Western blot analysis with these samples confirmed a significant increase of canonical histones compared to the levels of histone H2A.Z, a histone variant that is not regulated by Lsm1 as canonical histones (Figure 3c, Figure 3—figure supplement 3f).
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3c and quantification in Figure 3—figure supplement 3f.

claim: rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells display an aberrant nucleosome pattern with chromatin that is less accessible to MNase digestion.
source: rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells displayed a clear aberrant nucleosome pattern. While mono and di-nucleosomes were visible at concentrations ranging from 2.5 to 5 mU of Mnase in controls, chromatin from rad53-AID-lsm1-treated cells produced a high-molecular-weight smear that suggests that this chromatin is somehow less accesible to Mnase digestion.
evidence: This statement is supported by MNase digestion data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: High levels of histones are able to promote changes in chromatin structure.
source: Overall, our results indicate that the rad53-AID lsm1∆ system constitutes a good tool to generate conditional large accumulations of histones in the cell and that high levels of histones are able to promote changes in chromatin structure.
evidence: This statement is supported by MNase digestion data showing altered chromatin accessibility in Figure 3d.

claim: Live microscopy of rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells reveals a large majority of cells that arrest as large budded cells in which the nucleus migrates between the mother and the daughter cell.
source: We next sought to investigate if this system phenocopied some of the cell cycle defects observed in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector. Live microscopy and DAPI staining analysis of rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells reveals a large majority of cells that arrest as large budded cells in which the nucleus migrates between the mother and the daughter cell (Figure 3e and Figure 3—video 1 and 2)
evidence: This statement is supported by live microscopy data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells usually die after 6–8 hr of NAA treatment and are unable to enter or skip mitosis.
source: These cells usually died after 6–8 hr of NAA treatment and were unable to enter or skip mitosis.
evidence: This statement is supported by live microscopy observations.

claim: FACS analysis suggests that most rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells are able to complete replication.
source: FACS analysis suggested that most of them were able to complete replication (Figure 3f).
evidence: This statement is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3f.

claim: rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells treated for 4 hr with NAA exhibit a PFGE pattern similar to cells treated with Nocodazole and different from cells treated with Hydroxyurea.
source: Cells treated for 4 hr with NAA exhibited a similar pattern to the one observed in cells treated with Nocodazole and clearly different from the one observed in cells treated with Hydroxyurea that leads to the accumulation of cells that have not fully replicated their DNA (Figure 3g).
evidence: This statement is supported by PFGE data shown in Figure 3g.

claim: Treatment with Auxin specifically raises a population of rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells that had doubled their DNA content.
source: Treatment with Auxin specifically raised a population of cells that had doubled their DNA content (Figure 3h).
evidence: This statement is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3h.

claim: Cse4CENP-A lies at the centromere and is essential to recruit the kinetochore.
source: Cse4CENP-A and Htz1H2A.Z are two histone variants that can replace canonical histones H3 and H2A, respectively. Cse4CENP-A lies at the centromere and is essential to recruit the kinetochore (Stoler et al., 1995; Meluh et al., 1998; Fachinetti et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Htz1H2A.Z is enriched at the centromere and pericentromeric regions and is required for efficient chromosome segregation.
source: Htz1H2A.Z is enriched at the centromere and pericentromeric regions and is required for efficient chromosome segregation (Albert et al., 2007; Krogan et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Cse4CENP-A incorporation outside of the centromere region has been linked to WGDs in certain tumours.
source: Cse4CENP-A incorporation outside of the centromere region has been previously linked to WGDs in certain tumours (Tomonaga et al., 2003) and to aneuploidy in yeast (Castillo et al., 2007; Collins et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: High levels of Htz1H2A.Z incorporation at the pericentromeric region in yeast affects ploidy.
source: Similarly, high-levels of Htz1H2A.Z incorporation at the pericentromeric region in yeast also affected ploidy (Chambers et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Histone overexpression is able to promote changes in centromeric chromatin.
source: Since histone overexpression is able to promote changes in centromeric chromatin (Au et al., 2008; Castillo et al., 2007; Salzler et al., 2009; Takayama et al., 2010) we checked if high levels of histones were able to promote WGDs by changing the stoichiometry of canonical histones versus non-canonical histones at centromeric chromatin.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: High levels of histones do not change the amount of Cse4CENP-A at centromeres.
source: Analysis of several regions of chromosomes IV and XII revealed no changes in the amount of Cse4CENP-A at centromeres (Figure 4a, left panel).
evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Canonical histones increase their occupancy along several regions and are highly enriched at centromeres under high histone conditions.
source: Canonical histones in contrast did increase their occupancy along several regions and were highly enriched at centromeres (Figure 4a, middle and right panels).
evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Mtw1 recruitment to centromeres is similar in rad53-AID and rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells and does not significantly increase in other regions of the genome.
source: Mtw1 recruitment to centromeres IV and XII was similar and did not significantly increased in other regions of the genome.
evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4b and 4c.

claim: Most rad53-AID lsm1∆ arrested cells display one single mass of chromosomes in the daughter or mother cell that remains in line with the spindle axis.
source: As shown in Figure 4d, most of the arrested cells displayed one single mass of chromosomes in the daughter or the mother cell that always remained in line with the spindle axis.
evidence: This statement is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: Histone overexpression does not affect CENP-A recruitment, the attachment of kinetochores to chromosomes, or the attachment of both to the spindle.
source: We concluded that histone overexpression is able to increase histone H3 and H4 occupancy at centromeres and several other regions but this incorporation does not seem to affect CENP-A recruitment, the attachment of kinetochores to chromosomes, or the attachment of both to the spindle.
evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR and microscopy data shown in Figure 4.

claim: There is a clear decrease in the incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z to pericentromeric chromatin in rad53-AID lsm1∆ treated cells.
source: We next analysed the recruitment of Htz1H2A.Z to chromatin (Figure 5a). We observed a clear decrease in the incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z to pericentromeric chromatin in agreement with the global decrease of the H2AZ/H4 ratio shown in Figure 3c.
evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The decrease in Htz1H2A.Z incorporation is opposite to what was observed for histones H2B and H2A, indicating that Htz1H2A.Z molecules are being replaced by canonical histone H2A.
source: This decrease was opposite to what was observed for histones H2B and H2A and indicated that Htz1H2A.Z molecules were being replaced by the canonical histone H2A in the rad53-AID lsm1∆ mutant treated with Auxin.
evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The level of Htz1H2A.Z is decreased in wild-type cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector.
source: Interestingly, although wild-type cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector do not seem to increase the protein levels of H2B (see above Figure 1f), the level of Htz1H2A.Z was decreased in these cells (Figure 5b and c).
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5b and quantification in Figure 5c.

claim: Htz1H2A.Z overexpression largely increases the levels of Htz1H2A.Z in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector.
source: Htz1H2A.Z overexpression using a high copy vector largely increased the levels of Htz1H2A.Z observed in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector (Figure 5d)
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: Htz1H2A.Z overexpression decreases the amount of WGDs observed in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector.
source: Htz1H2A.Z overexpression using a high copy vector largely increased the levels of Htz1H2A.Z observed in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector (Figure 5d) and was able to decrease the amount of WGDs observed in these cells (Figure 5e).
evidence: This statement is supported by WGD quantification data shown in Figure 5e.

claim: Deletion of SWR1 increases the formation of WGDs in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG.
source: Consistent with the result of Figure 5e, deletion of SWR1, which decreases Htz1H2A.Z incorporation to chromatin (Mizuguchi et al., 2004) had an opposite effect to the one conferred by Htz1H2A.Z overexpression and increased the formation of WGDs in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG (Figure 5f).
evidence: This statement is supported by time course data shown in Figure 5f.

claim: Overexpression of Htz1H2A.Z in rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells is unable to suppress the defect in the incorporation of this histone variant to chromatin, the G2/M arrest or the lethality after NAA treatment.
source: Overexpression of histone Htz1H2A.Z in rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells also increased the amounts of total histone Htz1H2A.Z (Figure 5—figure supplement 5b) but was unable to supress the defect in the incorporation of this histone variant to chromatin, the G2/M arrest or the lethality after NAA treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1c, d ane e).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1c, d, and e.

claim: Htz1H2A.Z relative levels are important in the generation of WGDs in cells exposed to persistent transcription of histones H2A and H2B.
source: In summary, our results with the 2µ∆NEG vector indicate that Htz1H2A.Z relative levels are important in the generation of WGDs in cells exposed to a persistent transcription of histones H2A and H2B.
evidence: This statement is supported by data showing that H2A.Z overexpression reduces WGDs and SWR1 deletion increases WGDs in 2µ∆NEG cells.

claim: Excessive incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z to pericentromeric chromatin has been linked to WGDs.
source: Excessive incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z to pericentromeric chromatin has been previously linked to WGDs (Chambers et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: In S. pombe, Htz1H2A.Z is required to stabilize the recruitment of condensin to pericentromeres.
source: In S. pombe Htz1H2A.Z is required to stabilise the recruitment of condensin to pericentromeres, a complex able to embrace each of the daughter DNA strands and required to allow their proper segregation (Cuylen and Haering, 2011; Kim et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Depletion of the CAP-H kleisin subunit (Brn1) of Condensin II in drosophila S2 cells leads to chromosome segregation defects and produces a small number of abortive mitosis in which all genetic material is retained in one cell.
source: Depletion of the CAP-H kleisin subunit (Brn1) of Condensin II in drosophila S2 cells has been shown to lead to chromosome segregation defects and produce a small number of abortive mitosis in which all the genetic material is retained in one cell (Oliveira et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Mutations in the condensin II subunit Caph2 in mice have been involved in the generation of cells with increased ploidy content.
source: Mutations in the condensin II subunit Caph2 in mice have also been recently involved in the generation of cells with an increased ploidy content (Woodward et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Recruitment of Brn1 to pericentromeric chromatin decreases in three out of four pericentromeres examined in rad53-AID lsm1∆ treated cells.
source: Recruitment of Brn1 to pericentromeric chromatin decreased in three out of the four pericentromeres examined in five independent experiments suggesting that Htz1H2A.Z is important for condensin recruitment to pericentromeric regions in S. cerevisiae.
evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5g.

claim: Htz1H2A.Z is important for condensin recruitment to pericentromeric regions in S. cerevisiae.
source: Recruitment of Brn1 to pericentromeric chromatin decreased in three out of the four pericentromeres examined in five independent experiments suggesting that Htz1H2A.Z is important for condensin recruitment to pericentromeric regions in S. cerevisiae.
evidence: This statement is inferred from the observation that decreased H2A.Z incorporation correlates with decreased Brn1 recruitment.

claim: The smc2-8 mutant is extremely sensitive to histone overexpression.
source: The smc2-8 mutant, was extremely sensitive to histone overexpression (Figure 5h) further linking histone levels to condensin function.
evidence: This statement is supported by plate growth assay data shown in Figure 5h.

claim: Auxin treatment in rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells does not promote Pds1Securin phosphorylation.
source: Auxin treatment in rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells did not promote Pds1Securin phosphorylation (Figure 6a), a marker for DDR activation
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Auxin treatment in rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells does not enhance the formation of Mad2 foci at kinetochores.
source: Auxin treatment in rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells did not promote Pds1Securin phosphorylation (Figure 6a), a marker for DDR activation, or enhanced the formation of Mad2 foci at kinetochores, a marker used to detect SAC activation (Figure 6b).
evidence: This statement is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells show a slight stabilization of Pds1SECURIN during G2/M release.
source: This experiment revealed a slight stabilisation of Pds1SECURIN in rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells, higher levels of Scc1Rad21, the main substrate of Pds1, and Clb2 (Figure 6c and Figure 6—figure supplement 1a and b).
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: Clb2 starts to degrade but reaccumulates later in rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells, suggesting that APC-Cdh1 activity is impaired.
source: Clb2 started to degrade but reaccumulated later suggesting that the activity of APC-Cdh1 is impaired in this mutant.
evidence: This statement is inferred from the observation of Clb2 protein levels during the time course.

claim: Swe1WEE1 is stabilized in a hypophosphorylated form in rad53-lsm1∆-treated cells.
source: We next looked at Swe1WEE1 levels and observed that this kinase was stabilised in a hypophosphorylated form in rad53-lsm1∆-treated cells (Figure 6d).
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6d.

claim: Swe1WEE1 stabilization leads to higher levels of Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation that depend on Swe1WEE1.
source: This stabilisation led to a higher level of Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation that depend on Swe1WEE1 (Figure 6e)
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation in rad53-lsm1∆-treated cells is independent of the DDR, since MEC1 deletion does not abolish it.
source: This stabilisation led to a higher level of Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation that depend on Swe1WEE1 (Figure 6e) and was independent of the DDR, since MEC1 deletion did not abolish it (Figure 6f).
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6f.

claim: SWE1 deletion suppresses Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation but is unable to suppress Pds1 stabilization.
source: SWE1 deletion was able to suppress Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation but unable to suppress Pds1 stabilisation suggesting that the mechanism by which Pds1 is stabilised does not depend on Cdc28CDK1 activity (Figure 6g and Figure 6—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6g.

claim: The mechanism by which Pds1 is stabilized does not depend on Cdc28CDK1 activity.
source: SWE1 deletion was able to suppress Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation but unable to suppress Pds1 stabilisation suggesting that the mechanism by which Pds1 is stabilised does not depend on Cdc28CDK1 activity (Figure 6g and Figure 6—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This statement is inferred from the observation that SWE1 deletion does not suppress Pds1 stabilization.

claim: Cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector do not trigger Rad53CHK2 phosphorylation.
source: Cells transformed with this vector did not trigger Rad53CHK2 phosphorylation or enhanced the formation of Ddc2ATRIP foci, two common markers of the DNA damage checkpoint (Figure 7a and b).
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 7a.

claim: Cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector do not enhance the formation of Ddc2ATRIP foci.
source: Cells transformed with this vector did not trigger Rad53CHK2 phosphorylation or enhanced the formation of Ddc2ATRIP foci, two common markers of the DNA damage checkpoint (Figure 7a and b).
evidence: This statement is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 7b.

claim: Mad2 foci are slightly increased in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector, suggesting that the SAC could be activated.
source: The fact that Mad2 foci were slightly increased (Figure 7c) suggest that the SAC could be activated at least in some cells when histones are overexpressed.
evidence: This statement is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 7c.

claim: Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation is maintained for a longer time when histones are expressed in the rad53K227A strain.
source: This phosphorylation was only modestly affected in wild-type cells overexpressing histones (Figure 7d upper right panel) but was maintained for a longer time when histones were expressed in the rad53K227A strain (Figure 7d compare lower left and right panel).
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 7d.

claim: Cells exposed to high levels of histones are able to promote Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation, at least when Rad53 activity is impaired.
source: Cells exposed to high levels of histones seem to be able to promote a Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation, at least when Rad53 activity is impaired.
evidence: This statement is inferred from the observation that Cdc28 phosphorylation is prolonged in rad53K227A cells overexpressing histones.

claim: The Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation observed in rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells is directly related to the presence of high levels of histones.
source: This result suggest that the Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation observed in rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells is directly related to the presence of high levels of histones.
evidence: This statement is inferred from the observation that histone overexpression in rad53K227A cells prolongs Cdc28 phosphorylation.

claim: PDS1 deletion has only a slight effect on the cell cycle arrest observed in rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells.
source: PDS1 deletion had only a slight effect on the cell cycle arrest observed in rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells and did not significantly change the kinetics of diploidisation observed in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector (Figure 8—figure supplement 1a–c).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1a-c.

claim: MAD2 and SWE1 deletions accelerate the generation of WGDs in 2µ∆NEG transformed cells.
source: MAD2 and SWE1 deletions were able to accelerate the generation of WGDs in 2µ∆NEG transformed cells (Figure 8a)
evidence: This statement is supported by time course data shown in Figure 8a.

claim: MAD2 and SWE1 deletions do not change the ploidy content of cells transformed with an empty vector.
source: MAD2 and SWE1 deletions were able to accelerate the generation of WGDs in 2µ∆NEG transformed cells (Figure 8a) and did not change the ploidy content of cells transformed with an empty vector (Figure 8—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1d.

claim: MAD2 and SWE1 deletions have almost no impact on the cell cycle arrest observed in rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells individually but significantly suppress the arrest when combined.
source: These deletions had almost no impact on the the cell cycle arrest observed in rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells individually (Figure 8—figure supplement 1d) but significantly suppressed the arrest when combined (Figure 8b and Figure 8—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 8b and Figure 8—figure supplement 1d.

claim: WGD events observed upon histone overexpression are not generated by persistent activation of the DDR, the SAC, or stabilization of Swe1WEE1.
source: Overall, our results confirm that the WGD events observed upon histone overexpression are not generated by a persistent activation of the DDR, the SAC, or a stabilisation of Swe1WEE1.
evidence: This statement is inferred from the observation that checkpoint deletions accelerate rather than prevent WGDs.

claim: The SAC might cooperate with Swe1WEE1 to help prevent WGDs.
source: The results observed with Mad2 and Swe1WEE1 suggest that the SAC might instead cooperate with Swe1WEE1 and help to prevent them.
evidence: This statement is inferred from the observation that MAD2 and SWE1 deletions accelerate WGDs.

claim: High levels of histones interfere with chromosome segregation and promote WGDs.
source: In this study, we demonstrate that high levels of histones interfere with chromosome segregation and are able to promote WGDs.
evidence: This statement summarizes the main findings supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: WGDs induced by high histone levels are linked to a defect in the incorporation of histone variant Htz1H2A.Z.
source: Collectively, our results indicate that these events are linked to a defect in the incorporation of the histone variant Htz1H2A.Z.
evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR data showing decreased H2A.Z incorporation and genetic experiments showing that H2A.Z overexpression reduces WGDs.

claim: Increasing the levels of canonical histone H2A decreases the ratio H2A.Z/H2A in nucleosomes, thereby decreasing the interaction of H2A.Z with its readers.
source: We propose a competition model in which the canonical histone H2A competes with the histone variant H2A.Z. In this model, increasing the levels of canonical histone H2A will decrease the ratio H2A.Z/H2A in nucleosomes thereby decreasing the interaction of H2A.Z with the readers of this histone variant.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental observations.

claim: Histone overexpression has been shown to saturate certain histone-modifying enzymes.
source: Histone overexpression has been previously shown to saturate certain histone-modifying enzymes (Singh et al., 2010)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z and condensin requires nucleosome-free regions to be incorporated efficiently to chromatin.
source: Two reports have shown that the incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z (Ranjan et al., 2013) and condensin (Toselli-Mollereau et al., 2016) requires nucleosome-free regions to be incorporated efficiently to chromatin (Ranjan et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Regions where Htz1H2A.Z incorporation is decreased in rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells exhibit higher nucleosome occupancy and are less accessible to Micrococcal Nuclease digestion.
source: Our results show that the regions in which Htz1H2A.Z incorporation is decreased in rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells exhibit higher nucleosome occupancy and are less accessible to Micrococcal Nuclease digestion.
evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR and MNase digestion data.

claim: Accumulation of histones beyond replication might reduce the amount of nucleosome-free regions, which may explain why Htz1H2A.Z overexpression cannot suppress defects in rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells.
source: Accumulation of histones beyond replication might have a general effect on chromatin structure and reduce the amount of nucleosome-free regions. This general effect on chromatin structure may explain why the overexpression of Htz1H2A.Z is able to decrease the amounts of WGDs in cells overexpressing histones H2A and H2B but does not improve the incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z in rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells.
evidence: This is a proposed explanation based on experimental observations.

claim: Histone expression may be restricted to S-phase to avoid excessive incorporation of histones to chromatin and maintain nucleosome-free regions that promote specific incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z.
source: We infer from our results that histone expression may be restricted to S-phase to avoid an excessive incorporation of histones to chromatin and maintain nucleosome-free regions that would in particular promote the specific incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z (Boyarchuk et al., 2014; Nekrasov et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental results, supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Efficient incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z regulates condensin recruitment throughout the cell cycle.
source: Efficient incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z would regulate condensin recruitment throughout the cell cycle (Figure 9).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on experimental observations showing decreased condensin recruitment when H2A.Z incorporation is reduced.

claim: Condensin depletion has been linked to chromosome segregation defects and WGDs.
source: Condensin depletion has been previously linked to chromosome segregation defects and WGDs (Oliveira et al., 2005; Woodward et al., 2016) and could explain why high levels of histones promote WGDs.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Histone overexpression does not trigger the canonical DNA damage response.
source: Our results confirm that histone overexpression does not trigger the canonical DNA damage response.
evidence: This statement is supported by data showing no Rad53 phosphorylation or Ddc2 foci formation in cells overexpressing histones.

claim: The SAC could be activated in cells that overexpress histones, but this activation helps to prevent WGDs rather than causing them.
source: The Pds1 stabilisation observed in rad53-AID lsm1∆ treated cells added to the fact that MAD2 deletion enhances WGDs indicate that the SAC could be activated in cells that overexpress histones. This activation, however, does not seem to be the cause behind WGDs but rather a mechanism that helps to prevent them.
evidence: This statement is inferred from the observation that MAD2 deletion accelerates WGDs.

claim: Swe1WEE1 was previously reported to interact with histone H2B in yeast and humans, phosphorylate H2B at Tyr37 (Tyr40 in yeast), and promote efficient repression of histone transcription at the end of S-phase.
source: Swe1WEE1 was previously reported to interact with histone H2B in yeast and humans, phosphorylate H2B at Tyr37 (Tyr40 in yeast), and promote the efficient repression of histones transcription at the end of S-phase (Mahajan et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The stabilization of Swe1WEE1 in the presence of high levels of histones unveils an unsuspected and general role of Swe1WEE1 in histone metabolism.
source: The fact that this kinase is stabilised in the presence of high levels of histones unveils an unsuspected and general role of Swe1WEE1 in histone metabolism.
evidence: This statement is inferred from the experimental observation that Swe1 is stabilized under high histone conditions.

claim: Low levels of histone supply during S-phase delay mitosis in Drosophila embryos through increased CDK1 phosphorylation mediated by transcriptional downregulation of Cdc25 phosphatase.
source: Noteworthy, low levels of histone supply during S-phase have been shown to delay mitosis in Drosophila embryos through the increase of CDK1 phosphorylation levels mediated by the transcriptional downregulation of the Cdc25 phosphatase (Günesdogan et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Regulation of Cdc28CDK1 could be a mechanism by which cells respond to both high and low levels of histones.
source: Our results added to this study suggest that the regulation of Cdc28CDK1 could be a mechanism by which cells can respond to both high and low levels of histones.
evidence: This statement is inferred from the current findings combined with published literature.

claim: WGDs are frequently observed in cancer and play an important role in tumorigenesis.
source: WGDs are quite frequently observed in cancer (Zack et al., 2013) and play an important role in tumorigenesis (Davoli and de Lange, 2012; Dewhurst et al., 2014; Gordon et al., 2012; Janssen and Medema, 2013; Santaguida and Amon, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Overexpression of histone H2A has been linked to the transformation of normal liver to preneoplastic and neoplastic stages of Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
source: Overexpression of histone H2A has been linked to the transformation of normal liver to preneoplastic and neoplastic stages of Hepatocellular Carcinoma (Khare et al., 2011) where WGDs and aneuploidy are both frequent (Davoli and de Lange, 2011; Duncan et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Partial depletion of histone mRNA-binding factor SLBP leads to accumulation of abnormal levels of polyadenylated histone mRNAs beyond replication that can be translated and escape normal cell cycle control.
source: Two different lines of investigation, one in drosophila and one in bronchial cells, have shown that a partial depletion of the histone mRNA-binding factor SLBP leads to the accumulation of abnormal levels of polyadenylated histones mRNA beyond replication. These polyadenilated mRNAs can be translated and escape the normal cell cycle control of histones (Brocato et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: SLBP depletion in drosophila correlates with the generation of a tetraploid population.
source: In the first study, this depletion correlated to the generation of a tetraploid population (Salzler et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Arsenic partially depletes SLBP, which increases the tumorigenic potential of transformed cells.
source: The second study demonstrated that arsenic, a common carcinogenic agent able to promote aneuploidy and WGDs, partially depletes SLBP, which in turn increases the tumorigenic potential of transformed cells (Brocato et al., 2015; States, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Arsenic-induced cellular transformation induces a more compact chromatin structure.
source: Interestingly, arsenic-induced cellular transformation induces a more compact chromatin structure (Riedmann et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Histone deregulation might constitute an important and yet unexplored potential source of genome instability in cells.
source: Our work, combined with these reports, supports the idea that histone deregulation might constitute an important and yet unexplored potential source of genome instability in cells.
evidence: This statement is inferred from the current findings combined with published literature.

claim: Amplification of the small arm of chromosome 6, which contains 55 out of 65 genes encoding canonical histones, takes place in a wide variety of tumors and correlates with cancer aggressiveness.
source: It would therefore be interesting to revise upwards the amplification of the small arm of chromosome 6, which contains 55 out of the 65 genes that encode canonical histones. This amplification takes place in a wide variety of tumors and correlates with cancer aggressiveness (Santos et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.
